## Run code


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
2 + 2
sqrt(144)
```
:::


- `sqrt()` is a **function**. Inputs go in brackets.

## Objects


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
n_crimes <- 3445
n_areas <- 67
n_crimes / n_areas
```
:::


- `<-` stores a result in an **object**.

## Data frames

- Read data straight from the web:


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maczokni/crime_mapping_workshop/main/data/"
crimes <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "crimes.csv"))

nrow(crimes)
head(crimes)
table(crimes$crime_type)
```
:::


- Rows = crimes. Columns = variables.
- `$` picks one column.

## The pipe `|>` ("and then")


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
library(dplyr)

crimes |>
  filter(crime_type == "Robbery") |>
  count(outcome, sort = TRUE)
```
:::


- `filter()` keeps rows. `count()` tallies them.
- `==` compares. A single `=` doesn't.

## Your turn

Count **burglaries** by outcome.


::: {.cell setup='true' exercise='warmup_1'}
```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: warmup_1
library(dplyr)
crimes <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maczokni/crime_mapping_workshop/main/data/crimes.csv")
```
:::



::: {.cell exercise='warmup_1'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: warmup_1
crimes |>
  filter(crime_type == "______") |>
  count(______, sort = TRUE)
```
:::


::: {.hint exercise="warmup_1"}
`"Burglary"` (capital B). Count by `outcome`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="warmup_1"}
```r
crimes |>
  filter(crime_type == "Burglary") |>
  count(outcome, sort = TRUE)
```
:::

## Errors are normal


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
crimes |> filter(crime_type == "burglary") |> nrow()
Crimes |> nrow()
```
:::


- Line 1: 0 rows. R is case sensitive.
- Line 2: error. There's no `Crimes`, only `crimes`.
- Read the error. Search it online.
